news.title: LWN.net Weekly Edition for October 22, 2026
news.abstract: Welcome to the LWN.net Weekly Edition for October 22, 2026 This edition contains the following feature content: Vendor hooks in the Android kernel : a look at how Android deals with out-of-tree changes to the kernel. Hash-based module integrity for reproducible distributions : ideas on how to accommodate kernel-module integrity guarantees while still allowing reproducible builds. Safe self-referential data structures in kernel Rust : a possible way to remove unsafe Rust code related to lifetimes in the kernel. Recent and future changes to the Linux NFS server : an overview of new features added to the Linux implementation of NFS, as well as what may be coming soon. SUSE's efforts to disable setuid system-wide : Thorsten Kukuk has been working to improve security by enabling no_new_privs system-wide. Discussing a rewrite of XArray : a look at work to implement XArray in Rust. Cross-crate forward declarations in Rust : a proposal for cleaning up the kernel's handling of integer overflows in Rust code. Development statistics for the 7.3 kernel : the busiest development cycle in Linux history—so far. Understanding Nix flakes : a look at an experimental, but widely popular, Nix feature.
news.summary: 这期LWN周报并非单篇论文，而是专题汇编，涵盖Android内核厂商钩子、模块完整性与可复现构建、内核Rust安全自引用结构、XArray的Rust重写及Linux NFS服务器演进等。文章主要通过补丁提案解析和实现机制分析，讨论内核扩展、安全性及Rust化方向。现有内容未明确涉及网络子系统、eBPF/XDP、网卡驱动、容器网络数据面或DPDK/RDMA，NFS专题也未展示具体网络栈改动，故仅弱相关。
